title: The Mug That Became a Flowerpot
scene: At a pottery workshop, the narrator tries to make a coffee mug but widens the rim until it resembles a tiny flowerpot. A friend's gentle joke gives the failed mug a second purpose.
sceneJa: 陶芸体験でコーヒーマグを作るつもりが、夢中になって口を広げすぎ、植木鉢のような形に。友人の冗談をきっかけに、失敗作の使い道が見えてくる。

chunks.en: I was aiming for a coffee mug.
chunks.ja: コーヒーマグを作るつもりだと

chunks.en: making the rim wider and wider.
chunks.ja: 口の部分をどんどん広げてしまった
ようやく手を止めると
できあがった形はまるで
「小銭入れにすればいいじゃん」と

chunks.en: I said, picturing it on my desk.
chunks.ja: 机に置いた姿を想像しながら答えた

chunks.en: "It'll hold at least three coins," she added,
chunks.ja: 「少なくとも硬貨3枚は入るよ」と友人が続けたので
僕も認めざるを得なかった

questions.question: Which split keeps the result expression together?
options: When I finally / stopped it came / out looking like a tiny flowerpot.
When I finally stopped / it came out looking like / a tiny flowerpot.
When I finally stopped it / came out looking / like a tiny flowerpot.
questions.explanation: 'It came out looking like ...' describes the unexpected appearance of the finished piece. Keep 'came out looking like' together here.

questions.question: What does 'I was aiming for a coffee mug' mean?
options: The speaker wanted to make a coffee mug.
The speaker was throwing a mug at a target.
The speaker had already bought a mug.
questions.explanation: 'Aim for' means try to achieve a result. The intended result was a mug, not the flowerpot-like shape.

questions.question: Why does the speaker say 'I'll give you that'?
options: They are promising to give the pottery away.
They think their friend has insulted them seriously.
They reluctantly but playfully agree that the object could hold a few coins.
questions.explanation: 'I'll give you that' concedes a point. Here the speaker accepts the friend's tiny, funny consolation.

speak: Imagine: you are at a pottery class and your project looks different from your plan. Read: notice the expectation, accidental change, and gentle joke. Chunk: say 'I was aiming for', 'it came out looking like', and 'I'll give you that' as complete units. Understand: the first describes an intention, the second an outcome, and the third playful agreement. Check: answer the three questions. Speak (30 seconds): describe something you tried to make, what you were aiming for, what it came out looking like, and a friend's kind reaction. Final Read: read the six sentences aloud; stress 'aiming for', pause before 'a tiny flowerpot', and soften your voice on 'I'll give you that'.
review: New: 'I was aiming for ...'（〜を目指していた）, 'it came out looking like ...'（できあがると〜のように見えた）, 'I'll give you that'（その点は認める）. Reuse 'I got carried away' (Lesson 114) and 'On second thought' (Lesson 115) in a new hands-on arts context. The narrator does not win or solve a practical problem; they learn to accept a funny unintended result. Fictional story, no factual event claims. Dictionary references: https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/aim ; https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/come-out ; https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/give
